**Inertial Frame of Reference:**
A frame of reference in which Newton's first law of motion (the law of inertia) holds true. An unaccelerated frame (either at rest or moving with a constant velocity relative to other inertial frames).
*Example:* A spacecraft moving in deep space far away from gravitational fields at a constant velocity.

**Non-Inertial Frame of Reference:**
A frame of reference in which Newton's laws of motion do not hold true without introducing fictitious (pseudo) forces. An accelerating or rotating frame.
*Example:* A car accelerating forward or taking a sharp turn.
proTip: Fictitious forces like centrifugal force only appear in non-inertial frames.
